Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the VitalCore Medical Devices Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are David Larson, CEO; Sarah Jenkins, CFO; Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Technology Officer; and Michael Torres, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Larson.

David Larson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. VitalCore Medical Devices had a productive Q3, marked by significant advancements in our product portfolio and expansion into new markets.

Today, I will cover six key aspects of our performance:
1. Capital equipment vs consumables mix trends
2. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary
3. Strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter
4. Gross margin trends and supply chain commentary
5. Key assumptions underlying the guidance
6. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress

Sarah will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Chen will follow with updates on our R&D initiatives, and then we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with capital equipment versus consumables mix trends.

Our capital equipment and consumables revenue mix serves as a key indicator of the recurring revenue strength and long-term predictability in our business model, similar to the razor-and-blade approach that has propelled leaders like Intuitive Surgical with the da Vinci system or Medtronic with their Hugo robotic platform. In Q3, total revenue reached $1.28 billion, reflecting robust 14% organic growth year-over-year. By mix, capital equipment—such as our flagship CardioBot robotic-assisted PCI system and next-gen EchoFlex imaging suites—accounted for 38% of revenue, or $487 million, up 8% organically. Consumables—including PrecisionGuide catheters, BioShield stents, and EvoReel disposable kits—comprised the remaining 62%, or $793 million, surging 18% organically. This continues a shift where consumables have been our largest and fastest-growing segment for the seventh straight quarter.

Over the past three years, the consumables mix has grown from 52% in FY2021 to 59% in FY2022, and now 62% on a trailing twelve-month basis. This expansion stems from installed base growth, higher system utilization, and favorable ASPs on high-margin disposables. Our installed base ended Q3 with 2,450 CardioBot systems worldwide, up 22% year-over-year, driven by 185 new placements—our strongest quarter on record. EchoFlex ultrasound systems reached 1,120 units, up 15%. These installations generate ongoing revenue, with 95% attach rates for consumables in the first year post-install, akin to Stryker's Mako in orthopedics or Zimmer Biomet's ROSA robotics. CardioBot utilization averaged 28 procedures per system per week in Q3, up from 25 a year ago, boosted by our AI-driven software update in May that cuts setup time by 18% and increases OR throughput.

Consumable ASPs rose 6% year-over-year to $1,450 per procedure kit, aided by premium pricing on BioShield drug-eluting stents featuring proprietary nano-coating for 25% lower restenosis rates from our pivotal ROSA trial. Reimbursement pressures from CMS PCI bundle cuts trimmed 2 points off blended ASP growth, but value-based contracts with the top 20 IDNs have countered this with 3-year volume commitments at mid-single-digit premiums.

Regionally, in the U.S.—58% of Q3 revenue—consumables hit a record 65% mix, up from 61% last year, fueled by ASC procedure growth under MACRA and the No Surprises Act. Our CardioBot ASC penetration is now 32%, versus the 18% industry average per Definitive Healthcare, with $2.1 million annual consumable pull-through per system. EMEA showed a solid 60% consumables mix, boosted by CE Mark expansion for EvoReel kits into neurovascular, adding €45 million in revenue. APAC, our top-growth region at 25% organic, had consumables at 55% mix—up from 48%—driven by China NMPA approvals for CardioBot and a 40% installed base increase in private hospitals like Parkway Pantai. Japan pricing was flat due to chuikyo shinsa review, but 650 new procedures offset this.

Strategically, we're targeting a 65-68% consumables mix by FY2026 through the CardioBot 2.0 launch next quarter with modular arms for cardio, peripheral, and structural heart applications—expected to boost utilization 15-20% and expand our $4.2 billion TAM by 25%; a $150 million R&D push for single-use EchoFlex connectors aiming for 10% ASP uplift and lower cross-contamination risks post-COVID; and bundling pilots with payers like UnitedHealthcare guaranteeing 12% OR efficiency gains for shared savings.

For Q4, we anticipate consumables growth of 17-19% organic, with capital at 6-8% as we lap prior surges. Supply chain risks on polymer resins for stents are mitigated with 80% dual-sourcing from Sumitomo, though hospital capex caution in high-interest times could slow placements. Our $2.8 billion backlog, 70% consumable-weighted, offers strong visibility. This mix evolution highlights how capital opens doors while consumables fuel the flywheel, positioning us to exceed the 7-9% med device market growth per Evaluate MedTech, especially in robotics and minimally invasive procedures.

Now, let's talk about procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

Procedure volumes are the lifeblood of our structural heart, peripheral vascular, and electrophysiology businesses, and we're pleased with continued momentum as the industry normalizes post-pandemic. Globally, reported procedure volumes grew 14% year-over-year in Q3, the fifth straight quarter of double-digit increases, reaching 96% of pre-pandemic 2019 peaks, up from 88% in Q3 2023. Organically, excluding FX headwinds and prior inventory destocking in emerging markets, growth was 16%—outpacing consensus 10-12% med device recovery estimates from Leerink and Evercore—thanks to share gains in TAVR and LAAO.

By franchise, structural heart—45% of revenue—saw 18% volume surge. TAVR procedures, powered by our EvoFlex valve platform launched in the U.S. and Europe last fall, rose 22% globally. In the U.S., we hold 28% share ahead of Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien 3 Ultra, due to our lower-profile delivery and paravalvular leak rates under 2% from the INFINITY trial. Lower-risk FDA approvals have driven U.S. TAVR to 105% of 2019 levels. Transcatheter mitral repair volumes grew 15%, aided by our Abbott partnership on clip delivery, while watching their Tendyne platform.

Peripheral vascular interventions rose 12%, with 20% rebound in BTK procedures from diabetes trends. Our Tack Endovascular System for dissections grew 25%, backed by STAPLE trial data at SCAI showing 95% 12-month patency. DCBs accelerated post-Lutonix expansion.

EP volumes increased 9% amid U.S. cath lab staffing issues, but our PFA platform—with CE Mark and U.S. IDE enrollment—promises 30% faster cases under 90 minutes, appealing to centers like Cleveland Clinic.

Neuromodulation grew 11%, led by 16% in spinal cord stimulators as payers like UnitedHealthcare broaden coverage for high-frequency therapies like Nevro's HF10.

Regionally, U.S. (55% of volumes) grew 17% to 102% of 2019, with electives recovered via easing staffing (nurse vacancies at 12% per AHA) and CY2024 OPPS preserving EvoFlex pass-through. Outpatient TAVR hit 25% of cases, with 45% same-day discharges.

Europe (25%) grew 9% to 92% of 2019, hampered by German/French reimbursement caps at €28,000 for TAVR, but our DiGital Health AI planning secured preferred status in 60% of top German centers. UK up 14% post-NICE LAAO guidance.

APAC (15%) shone at 22%, China +28% with EvoFlex NMPA and Shanghai manufacturing; targeting 20% share by 2025 via MicroPort JV. Japan +15% with PMDA PFA.

Emerging markets +10%, Brazil clearing backlogs.

Recovery is maturing: pent-up demand exhausted (U.S. TAVR waitlists -40%), but demographics (65+ up 3% YoY) and comorbidities (diabetes 11.6% per CDC) drive growth. OR utilization at 85% per Definitive Healthcare. Labor shortages persist (2,500 U.S. electrophysiologists vs. 3,000 needed).

We're investing $250 million in FY24 capex for robotics/AI: Intuitive da Vinci integration for hybrid TAVR (15% faster in 50 U.S. pilots), EchoSense AI cutting planning to 24 hours. Supply chain onshored 90% post-2022 shortages.

We expect Q4 volumes at 12-15%, full-year organic 13-15%, with share gains offsetting Europe pricing. Risks: Medicare Advantage scrutiny, China VBP—but PFA U.S. launch mitigates. Positioned for $200 billion med device market by 2027 per Grand View.

Moving on to strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter.

As we close a strong Q3 with 12% revenue growth to $1.28 billion—driven by 18% organic in structural heart and resilience in orthopedics—our Q4 priorities center on accelerating innovation, optimizing global footprint, and sustainable profitability in a 5.2% CAGR market through 2028 per Grand View, fueled by demographics and procedural shifts.

Four pillars: (1) Pipeline acceleration and launches, (2) Geographic expansion, (3) Operational excellence, (4) Emerging tech investments.

First, pipeline: In structural heart (35% revenue), full U.S. ramp of VitalFlow TAVR post-FDA, targeting 30-35% volume growth to 15,000 procedures with 20% field force to 450 reps, deepening Cleveland Clinic-like ties. CoreClip mitral repair pivotal trials readout quarter-end vs. Abbott's 65% dominance.

Neuromodulation: Infinity DBS for Parkinson's at 22% Q3 growth vs. 15% industry; Q4 AI closed-loop software for 40% adoption in 50,000+ base. Orthopedics steady 8-10%, mid-teens on Trinity robotic knee vs. Stryker Mako.

Second, expansion: U.S. 60% revenue, but 25% of $150 million Q4 capex international. Europe: EU MDR complete for 90%, 20% sales force in Germany/France for 16-18% EMEA growth vs. 12% market, +300 bps share vs. Medtronic Concerto.

APAC 25%+ FY24: $50 million China localization for VitalPace Nano pacemaker vs. NMPA, 40% conversions in Tier-1 pilots. India/Brazil 30% on affordable ortho.

Third, operations: 70% critical components dual-sourced (nickel-titanium), lead times -35% to 12 weeks. Gross margins 68-70% via Greenfield automation (+15% throughput). SG&A flat at 28%, R&D 12%, FCF $300 million.

Fourth, tech: $80 million AI/ML for VitalSense RPM wearable post-TAVR (95% Epic/Cerner integration, $15 billion market 28% CAGR McKinsey). Blockchain for stent traceability in APAC.

These support Q4 revenue $1.25-1.28 billion, 8-10% growth, 15%+ EPS.

Next, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary.

We achieved a strong 67.2% gross margin in Q3, up 140 bps YoY from 65.8% and 110 bps sequentially from Q2's 66.1%, with TTM at 66.8%—above our 65-68% target and peers like Boston Scientific (68%) and Stryker (65%).

Drivers: Product mix +80 bps, neurovascular (FlowSense stents, CerebraFlow coils) up 22% YoY to 28% revenue at 75% margins, from stroke volumes and CMS thrombectomy reimbursements. Commodity guidewires declined in mix.

Pricing +50 bps: 2.5-3% hikes on VasoTrack cath lab products, low pushback with 18% U.S. EP share, like Abbott's structural heart power.

COGS inflation -30 bps from 12% resin (polycarbonate/PEEK) and 8% freight (Red Sea), but 70% hedging limited to 1.5% over guidance.

Q4 margins 67.5-68.0%, FY24 67.0%, assuming robotics ramp (NeuroArm for da Vinci, +15% growth).

Supply chain: Inventory 7.2 months (up YoY, stable seq), no disruptions unlike EtO peers. Geopolitics +15% electronics, titanium +10%.

Initiatives: 35% catheter sourcing to Mexico/Vietnam (-22% lead times, Tijuana JV -11% costs); PolyMed acquisition insources 40% polymers (+5% yields, $12M savings); AI maintenance in Galway/San Diego (+95% utilization, -18% stent scrap).

U.S. (72% revenue): 85% domestic under QMSR, post-Change Healthcare restocking. Europe (18%): 95% MDR pass, UK freeports. APAC (10%): Singapore local mfg.

Sustainability: Recyclable elastomers in 20% disposables (-7-9% costs, Vizient appeal). $150M capex for additive mfg (+5-7% margins by 2026).

This execution fortifies outperformance.

Then, key assumptions underlying the guidance.

Our FY2025 guidance is $12.8-13.2 billion revenue, 8-11% reported/7-10% organic growth. Bottom-up from iData, IQVIA, Deloitte, modeling 140+ products.

Top line: Mid-single-digit volumes, U.S. +5-7% on electives/demographics (65+ +3%). TAVR +9-11% on Evolut FX+ (28% share per CRT), lower-risk EARLY trial. EP ablations +6-8% on DiamondTemp (15% faster lesions).

Pricing flat to +1%: U.S. stable CMS 2025 OPPS (+2.9%, pass-throughs incl. EluNIR stent); int'l Japan/Australia tailwinds offset China 2% erosion (6 NMPA H1 incl. robotic endoscopy).

Regions: U.S. 9-12% (55%, +6% same-store); EMEA 5-7% (95% MDR compliant vs. Medtronic delays); APAC 10-13% (China 15%+ Watchman FLX 20% share, India Persona IQ); LATAM 8%.

Gross 68-69% (+50 bps midpoint, supply norm, Galway AI +12% yields). OpEx +7-8%, R&D 12.5% ($1.6B, 15 Phase III incl. Algovita SCS vs. Abbott/Medtronic).

Levers: $500-700M buybacks (15x P/E), 2 M&A $300-500M digital (HeartFlow-like). FX: +1% EUR, -2% JPY.

Sensitivities: 1% U.S. volume = $100M rev; labor -200 bps growth; robotics +$200M. High rates delay capex, 65% recurring buffers; inflation >3% -50 bps margins.

Embeds 5.5% industry growth +200 bps outperformance.

Finally, R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

R&D is our lifeblood for leadership in the $500B+ medtech market amid raw material inflation and semiconductor issues. Q3 spend $485 million, 13.1% of sales (up from 11.8% YoY, 17% increase), FY $1.9-2.0B (40% new products, 35% sustaining/clinical, 25% digital/AI). Above peers (Boston Sci 11%, Medtronic 9-10%), targeting high-margin disruption.

28 active programs, 12 late-stage (up from 9). Milestones: FDA IDE for VitaFlow TAVR (polymer leaflets, 20% durability vs. Sapien 3; 45 sites, 500 subjects, zero PVL early). NeuroPulse SCS (AI adaptive, 65% pain relief vs. 45% Intellis; IDE complete 320 pts, PMA submitted, H2 2025 U.S., Germany DiGA reimbursement).

U.S. (55% pipeline): Breakthrough for 3 assets incl. AI cath -30% fluoro. Europe (25%): OrthoGuide RX launch 12 countries, 15% knee share vs. Mako. APAC (20% up from 15%): China NMPA wearable glucose/ketone with Mindray ($10B diabetes); Japan JV endometrial ablation.

Megatrends: Value-based (60% RWE, cloud pacemakers -25% readmits); AI/digital twins ($150M Boston NVIDIA CoE, -40% prototyping); sustainability (Phase II bioresorbable stents plant polymers vs. EU MDR).

2025: 4 launches, $400-500M peak rev, $15B NPV. Risks: trial delays, CMS cuts—but 45% new product margins cushion for 15-18% 3-year growth.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah for a review of our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins:
Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we delivered a solid financial performance this quarter. Total revenue was $1.28 billion, up 14% reported and organic, driven by the consumables strength and procedure growth he outlined. Breaking it down, U.S. was 58% at 16% organic growth, EMEA 24% at 11%, APAC 18% at 25%. Gross profit came in at $860 million, yielding that 67.2% margin David discussed, with operating expenses at 28% of revenue, reflecting disciplined SG&A and R&D investments. Adjusted operating income rose 20% to $320 million, EPS expanded 18% to $0.85. We generated $250 million in operating cash flow, ending with $2.8 billion in cash and a net debt to EBITDA of 1.8x.

For Q4, we guide revenue $1.25-1.28 billion, 8-10% growth; full-year organic 12-13%. Adjusted gross margin 67.5-68%, OpEx 28-29% of sales, EPS $3.40-3.50, implying 16% growth. FY2025 as David noted, $12.8-13.2 billion. These reflect conservative procedure and pricing assumptions amid macro caution, but with upside from pipeline.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Chen for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Emily Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. We are making significant progress in our R&D efforts. Particularly excited about our ongoing clinical trials for the VitaFlow TAVR, which is showing promising results in reducing calcification and improving long-term durability. Building on David's overview, our pipeline remains robust with key advancements in PFA for EP, NeuroPulse SCS, and robotics integrations. We've hit enrollment milestones and regulatory nods across regions, positioning several assets for 2025 launches that will expand our TAM in structural heart and neuromodulation. Our investments are yielding real clinical differentiation, like faster procedures and better patient outcomes, as evidenced in recent trial data.

Now, back to David for Q&A.

David Larson:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from Laura Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen - JPMorgan:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. David, on the capital-consumables mix, with CardioBot 2.0 coming, how do you see utilization evolving, and any risks to ASPs from bundling pilots?

David Larson:
Great question, Laura. CardioBot 2.0's modular design should drive 15-20% utilization lift by enabling multi-specialty use, building on the current 28 procedures per week. We've seen similar gains with software updates before. On ASPs, bundling with UnitedHealthcare locks in premiums via efficiency guarantees, offsetting any CMS pressures—our value-based contracts have held mid-single-digit uplifts. No major risks; backlog visibility is strong.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel - Goldman Sachs:
Thanks. Sarah, can you expand on the FY2025 guidance assumptions, particularly FX and M&A impact?

Sarah Jenkins:
Sure, Mike. FX at current spots adds a slight tailwind, +1% Euro offsetting -2% Yen. M&A assumes two bolt-ons in digital health, $300-500 million total, accretive from day one via pipeline synergies like AI imaging. Sensitivities remain as outlined: volumes are the biggest driver. We're confident in the midpoint given share gains.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim - Bank of America:
Hi team. On procedure recovery, Michael, how is commercial execution driving U.S. ASC penetration, and EMEA reimbursement outlook?

Michael Torres:
Thanks, Rachel. ASC shift is key—our 32% CardioBot penetration reflects rep training on outpatient workflows and EvoFlex's same-day discharge profile. We're targeting 40% by year-end via IDN partnerships. EMEA reimbursements are stabilizing; DiGital Health AI secured preferred status, and UK NICE helps. Growth will accelerate as volumes hit 100% of 2019.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Evercore. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly - Evercore:
Good morning. Dr. Chen, on the R&D pipeline, any updates on NeuroPulse PMA timeline or China approvals?

Dr. Emily Chen:
Tom, NeuroPulse PMA is on track for H2 2025 approval, with strong IDE data on pain relief superiority. China NMPA for the wearable glucose/ketone monitor is approved, partnering with Mindray for scale. These de-risk the APAC ramp and align with diabetes megatrends.

David Larson:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are well-positioned to continue our growth trajectory and deliver long-term value.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
